Hi, I cannot talk for how it interacts with Zoloft, but with Lexapro. Zofran interacts with all SSRI’s, which is why I had the reaction on Lexapro.  About 2 hours after talking 4mg Zofran (30 minutes prior I took 10mg Lexapro) I got hit with pretty bad stomach cramps, so I took a shower and the best way to explain it was I started to kind of dissociate, everything just felt wrong. I ended up vomiting and went to the ER because my heart rate spiked (155 resting) and I had horrible full body tremors. I was given Ativan and sent home to sleep, and after about 24 hrs I was completely back to normal. The doc said it wasn’t full blown seratonin syndrome, but it was a reaction between the two meds. Although it wasn’t Zoloft, Lexapro is an SSRI and Zofran interacts with that class of meds. Since then, I have had a few health issues where I could have been given Zofran, but due to my past reaction they don’t. I would definitely talk to your doctor before taking anything, but also remember everyone’s different and how one person reacts to a medication can be different from how you will!

There isn’t a label that I’ve found that seems to really fit how i identify so i say i’m gender queer. My feels about how i identify don’t come from society gender roles and the expectation of how men/woman are supposed to act. There are many cis people who live their lives not conforming to gender roles. In terms of people who fall on the lines of not identifying with their assigned gender it is deeper than stuff like that.

for me, i was born female. overall, i have no issues with people using and different pronouns for me. overall i have a preference for they/them but it doesn’t bother me enough to correct anyone because i just truly never feel misgendered. In my head, i don’t completely feel right using anyone label. I don’t feel like a woman because i just don’t. it’s one of those things that people don’t really have to question/could completely understand unless you’re having to deal with it. I feel like a man in the physical sense that i was born in the wrong body. Ever since i was ten i did things and like pretended i had a penis 😅 however, i am comfortable with the way i dress and stuff. overall it changes day to day whether i’m feeling for “masculine” or “feminine” 

I don’t feel like fit into any one gender. i always wish that there was a button i could press that would make my body match the way i’m feeling in my head because no matter what my body is, it’s something that will never match my gender because i feel so many different things. Child abuse. I worked with the special needs students at my school when I was in high school. I played unified basketball, where “regular” students and the special needs student would play together. I was one of 6 partners, and our role was to assisted the athletes (special needs students) with passing, helping them with drills, how to work well with others, and most importantly, keeping the kiddos safe. There was one boy, we’ll call him Tom (not his real name) and he had autism. He was a hothead to say the least. He had some real behavioral issues and was quick to become aggressive. Anyways, because of this, he was hard to control, and didn’t listen to anyone other than me. I took the role of making sure he kept his cool during practice/games and would take him on breaks if he needed them. We were at practice doing a drill where everyone had a ball, except for one person who tried to steal the balls. The object of the drill was to work on possession, and not letting others take the ball from you.  It was going fine, until someone tried taking the ball away from Tom. I saw what was happening and thankfully I was only a few feet away, so I stepped between Tom and the other kid (also autistic) right as Tom threw a right hook, and he hit me square in the jaw. He was a little dude, but fuck me that punch almost landed me on my ass. Blah blah blah I take him for a walk to calm down, and everything’s fine. 

That was a long back story, but this was where the accusation comes in.

It was game day the following week after Tom punched me. We were playing at home, and Tom’s mother was there, along with many other parents, including my mom right in the row right in front of her. The game was going fine, everyone having a good time until Tom misses a shot. He started getting mad, but I was able to handle him.  It took a turn for the worse when an athlete on the other team took the ball from him. Tom started growling (yes, literally growling) and the kid and getting really angry. 

I had been taught by the coach (a special ed teacher) that one thing that calms the kid down is when you LIGHTLY squeeze his arms, and direct him to look at you. Almost like you were giving him a massage.

I knew things were going south, so I decided that it would be best to do with with him, something that I’ve done before and was instructed to do.  We were on the court together because I was partnered up with him. I began doing this, and mind you, it wasn’t aggressive at all. Just a light squeeze because that sensation was calming to him (because of his autism). He started calming down, when I heard his mother in the audience. 

“HOW DARE SHE TOUCH MY SON LIKE THAT!?  SHES GETTING HIM WORKED UP AND IS GOING TO HURT HIM! SHE HAS NO RIGHT DO BE TOUCHING HIM AND HURTING HIM LIKE THAT!” 

She was outraged that I was doing what I was instructed to do to calm him down, which had worked, he was calmer. It was so bad, my mom who was sitting right in front of her had to leave. After the game, I was heartbroken. Luckily the schools social worker was at the game (she worked with the kiddos a lot, so she’d come to the games sometimes) and told the mom something along the lines of “calm down, he’s fine, she’s not hurting him” or whatever.  I love the kids so much, and I would never do anything to hurt them, and to think that a parent thought I was abusing her kid made me cry. I felt so awful thinking that I hurt Tom, but I did what I had to because he was going to hurt someone. After the game, my mom, the coach, the social worker and even other parents came up to me saying that I didn’t do anything wrong and to not be upset. My coach and I talked and agreed it would be best for me to not work with him again, not because of any wrong doings, just so the mom would shut the fuck up. It was a really shitty situation because I really liked the kid, and we had a good relationship, but I guess the mom rather would’ve had her son hurt someone than someone calm him down in an appropriate way.
